title: Shrimp and vegetables without carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy greens; no potatoes, soy‑based sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Shrimp are a high‑protein seafood with low fat and rich in trace minerals such as iodine and selenium. The vegetables used in this dish can include bell pepper, zucchini, mushrooms, onion and tomato, providing a range of vitamins and minerals while excluding carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy greens, potatoes and soy‑based sauce.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shrimp can change shell color depending on water temperature.
A 100 g serving of shrimp provides about 20 g of protein, making it an excellent protein source.
Vegetables like zucchini and bell pepper are high in vitamin C, which enhances iron absorption from seafood.
Shrimp contain astaxanthin, a powerful antioxidant that gives them their pink hue.
Steaming vegetables preserves most of their nutrients.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Shrimp deliver easily digestible protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: 100 g of shrimp contain roughly 85 kcal, making the dish suitable for weight management.

items.title: Source of iodine and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals support thyroid function and antioxidant defenses.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals from vegetables
items.content: Bell pepper provides vitamins C and A, zucchini offers potassium and vitamin B6, mushrooms supply vitamin D and iron.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Low saturated fat and the presence of omega‑3 fatty acids in shrimp promote heart health.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain cholesterol, so people with hypercholesterolemia should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Pesticide residues on vegetables
items.content: Wash raw vegetables thoroughly to reduce pesticide residues.

items.title: Sodium in prepared sauces
items.content: Avoid soy‑based sauces, as they can add a high amount of salt.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sauté shrimp over medium heat for 2‑3 minutes until pink, then add sliced vegetables (bell pepper, zucchini, mushrooms, onion, tomato) and cook another 5‑7 minutes until tender. Finish with a splash of lemon juice and fresh herbs if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh shrimp refrigerated and use within 2 days; store the cooked dish in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Keep vegetables in a separate bag in the fridge to prevent excess moisture.
